submission.justification: Recommend Radiator-R1 at 4 cm. The simulation scan shows this gives the best pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c among all allowed candidates and thicknesses tested: 4.748 sigma. It outperforms the next-best option, Radiator-R3 at 3 cm with 3.838 sigma, by 0.91 sigma. R1 is also reported lifetime-acceptable, and 4 cm lies within the required 1–6 cm thickness range. Performance peaks near 4 cm and decreases at larger thicknesses, so increasing beyond 4 cm is not beneficial.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c.
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1 at 4 cm has the highest simulated separation, 4.748 sigma. Best alternatives are R3 at 3 cm with 3.838 sigma and R2 at 3 cm with 3.006 sigma.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1 is one of the three allowed candidates; recorded allowed flags show R1, R2, and R3 are all allowed.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must keep its performance over the experiment's lifetime.
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1_lifetime_acceptable = 1. No candidate was excluded by lifetime constraints, and dry nitrogen flush operation is recorded.
Selected thickness is 4 cm, which is within the allowed 1–6 cm range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended radiator and thickness.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one recommendation: Radiator-R1 with thickness 4 cm.
